Senses.Note: Zen bends an ordinary death-and-revival image into a stock saying repeatedly quoted in teaching-seat discourse and biographies. It belongs with ‘let go at the cliff’ (懸崖撒手), ‘the life-root is severed’ (命根斷), and ‘gain life within death’ (死中得活), but remains one figurative referent rather than separate literal and technical objects. Frozen-corpus concordance: 254 exact hits in 132 storage files representing 131 independent works.

Senses.Explanation: To revive after being cut off: the records use a death-and-revival image in a recurrent teaching-seat formula and in explicit criticism of that formula. Its dominant fixed formula is ‘let go at the cliff and personally assent and undertake it; revive after being cut off, and you cannot deceive anyone’ (懸崖撒手，自肯承當；絕後再甦，欺君不得). Records also place it after ‘the life-root is severed’ (命根斷), beside ‘shed skin and exchange bones’ (去皮換骨), and compare it with a cold ember flaming and a withered tree flourishing again. Tianqi Benrui explicitly departs from the inherited formula: ‘the former sages all wanted to revive after being cut off; I am not like that.’ The entry reports this recurrent sequence and its criticism without deciding what state the phrase denotes.
